description: Since Inspector Rook took an interest in the tip, the Gaugers walk Rustmoor in pairs at dusk, in good boots, writing down who is picking where. They stop nobody. They do not need to. Tonight a pair is working along the crane gantry towards your heap, and your heap, like every heap in Rustmoor, has a fair amount of Board paperwork in it.

options.label: Keep picking in plain view, and let them write down whatever they like.

success.text: The Gaugers stop at your heap and watch you sort umbrella ribs from bedsprings for some minutes. One of them writes. The other asks, politely, how the picking is. You tell her. They move on. Somewhere on Gaugehill a file grows a page thicker, and somewhere else Rook reads that you did not run.

options.label: Slip down among the chain-anchors and wait in the dark for them to pass.

success.text: You know the tip better than its visitors do. You fold yourself between two anchor-plates and listen to good boots go by overhead, unhurried, and fade towards the gate. When you climb back up, your heap is exactly as you left it. Nobody has written anything down.

failure.text: The anchor-plate you choose is greased, and you arrive at the bottom of it rather faster than planned, with a noise like a coal delivery. A lantern finds you. A Gauger asks if you are hurt and writes the answer down, along with your name, the time and the anchor's number.

options.label: Gather up the Board paperwork in your heap and hand it to them, unread.

success.text: The Gaugers take the bundle with thanks and a receipt. They seem pleased, and puzzled, and they walk on without writing anything down about you at all. The pickers at the next heap saw the whole thing, and the pickers at the next heap go home to the Lowvents.
